Better ID photos: enhancing, lining up faces, and a report of photos that need checking.

### What's changed
- **Photo names can have other words in them.** A photo called *Jane Doe ID Photo Good.jpg* is matched to Jane Doe when you import or update in bulk, as long as the first and last name are next to each other.
- **Enhance photos.** The new **Enhance** button in the person editor improves a dark, dull or grainy photo, and **Undo enhance** puts it back. It never changes skin tone or colours.
- **Line up faces.** Everyone's face can be the same size and in the same place on their card, however the photo was taken. The face finder is part of the program and runs on this PC, with nothing sent anywhere.
- **New Settings → Photos:** *Enhance photos that need it* and *Line up faces on every card*. Both work for photos added one at a time, by import and by bulk update. **Both are off to start**, so cards look as they did until you turn them on.
- **Photos that need checking are reported.** People whose photo is missing, turned away, too close-up, too small or poor are labelled in the list, can be shown with **Show → Needs checking**, and are listed at the end of an import or bulk update.
- **Big imports and bulk updates go one person at a time** with a progress window, so the PC isn't overloaded.
- Large camera photos are shrunk more sharply.
- The screens are tidier: even spacing, matching buttons, and Settings back in two columns.
- Fixed an error in the person editor for a client with no card template.

Existing installs keep all their templates, clients, people and settings.

### Updating
An administrator will see **Version 3.0.15 is available** at the top of the program — choose **Update now**. Or download the setup below and run it over the top.

### New install
Download **ID-Card-Printing-Software-Free-Setup-3.0.15.exe** below and run it. The setup isn't code-signed, so the first time Windows may show *Windows protected your PC*: choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**, then **Yes**.
